partitor 0.13.0

From score to parts

Turn a score PDF into large-print parts. You work in a terminal. Make every change first, review, then build once. Only the build takes long.

  1. 1DropPDF into the inbox
  2. 2Analyseproof of who plays what, 1–5 min
  3. 3Editnames, choices, groups, layout
  4. 4Reviewone screen, every setting
  5. 5Buildthe part PDFs, minutes

Dashed: the stages that take time. You can go back from Review to Edit as often as you like. Nothing is built until you build.

Before you start

What you need

  • A score PDF: vector (from notation software) or a scan. Scans at 300 dpi greyscale work best.
  • A library folder with two folders inside, inbox and library. You put score PDFs in inbox. partitor writes everything else in library. See STORAGE-LOCAL.md or STORAGE-SMB.md.
System Status Start command
Linux (Ubuntu LTS) supported sudo partitor (partitor as root)
Windows (PowerShell) experimental partitor
macOS (Terminal) best effort see Advanced

Install once: INSTALL.md on Linux, the setup program from the Download page on Windows. Where this guide says “run partitor”, use the start command of your system. On Windows, type \ in paths.

Linux library: /var/lib/partitor/library. Windows library: Documents\partitor.

One command. Type partitor and press Enter. Everything else is a menu: answer with a number or a letter. Enter accepts the value in [brackets]. q stops and keeps what is done.

Stage 1

Drop the PDF in the inbox

  1. Copy the score PDF into inbox.
  2. Run partitor. The menu lists the pieces, newest first, and n new from inbox (1 waiting).
  3. Press n, the number of the PDF, then the pages of the piece. Enter takes all pages. Type a range such as 8-9 when the PDF holds several pieces.

The PDF moves into a new item folder in the library, named by its id: 2026-10-0001 (year, month, number).

Stage 2 · takes 1–5 minutes

Analyse and check the proof

partitor reads every page. It makes no parts yet. When it ends, open the proof:

library/2026-10-0001-bach-example-piece/2026-10-0001-proof.pdf

The proof

  • Each proof page is a score page.
  • Each system has a blue name, for example p8.s2 (page 8, system 2).
  • Each staff shows its part. Follow one part down the pages: it must continue without gaps.

Red frame. partitor is not sure of a system in a red frame. Its staves show ? name, the suggestion. You answer these in stage 3.

To analyse again, press y in the item menu, or run partitor analyse ID.

Stage 3

Edit: names, choices, layout

The wizard asks these in order. Each answer is saved at once. Nothing is built. Press q to stop and come back later.

Title and composer

Title, composer (full name, as printed on page 1), then the short form for the page heads (suggested: the surname). Change them later with m.

Part names

The names come from the printed staff labels. Type one change at a time. Press Enter when done.

Type Does
7=Organ renames part 7
7=- no PDF for part 7 (listed as “not extracted”)
7=+ makes the PDF for part 7 again
7+8 joins part 7 into part 8: one part on two staves
7=-; 8=Continuo several changes in one line

Choices for the red systems

For each uncertain system the wizard shows its position, its clefs and labels, and the suggestion as part numbers. Type one part number per staff, top staff first.

[1/9] p8.s2: source page 8, system 2 of 4 from the top (proof page 8) 3 staves, clefs top to bottom: F4 G2 F4 suggestion: Bass Trombone, Continuo, Continuo (= 6 7 7) part number for each of the 3 staves, top first (Enter = suggestion; 0 = leave out; same number twice = one part on two staves; j = join with the system below): 6 7 7
Answer Does
Enter takes the suggestion
0 leaves the staff out
same number twice one part on two staves
j joins this system with the one below
d drops the whole system
q stops. Continue with r in the item menu

A corrected answer becomes the suggestion for the next systems with the same clefs. The proof is drawn again after each answer. More: Advanced.

Bar numbers

The wizard asks only when it needs to. After a short first bar: p pickup (Enter), i incipit, n neither. When a repeat splits a bar: Y or n. Check a few numbers against the proof. Corrections: Advanced.

The item menu

Open it at any time: run partitor, then type the number of the item. The status line lists what changed since the last build.

Key Edit (saved, not built)
m title, subtitle, composer
t part names
g groups
n bar numbers and rehearsal marks
e / c larger / smaller staves
p number of pages
a paper: Letter, A4, Ledger
k ambitus of a part
h short names of staves in a group score
u cue lines
s any setting as key=value
Key Other
v review (stage 4)
y analyse again. Names, groups and settings stay
f fit: paper and staff size for the best page turns
l pages of a built part, with the turn after each
x repage: new page breaks, no new analysis
r build (stage 5)
b back to the list

Details of these keys: Advanced.

Stage 4

Review everything

Press v in the item menu, or run partitor show ID. The wizard shows this screen before “Build now?”.

The review screen

2026-10-0001 · Example piece · 7 parts · ready to build status: ready to build title: Example piece composer: J. S. Bach short: Bach (from the composer) parts: 1 Canto (G2) — ambitus E4-G5 2 Alto Trombone (C3) — ambitus F3-A4 4 Tenor Trombone I (C4) — ambitus C3-F4 (by hand) 7 Continuo (G2+F4) — two staves, ambitus none (off) group: Trombones: Alto Trombone, Tenor Trombone I, … bars: line starts 1, 3, 6, 9 …; letters A (p10.s3) settings: paper=letter

Check the parts, the groups and the title. If something is wrong, go back to stage 3. Nothing is built yet.

Ambitus. The lowest and highest note of each part, printed before the first line. The proof rings them in green, with bar, page and system. Check them. Fix a wrong value with k.

Status Means Next
not analysed the analysis did not finish y or r
needs choices red systems still open r asks them first
ready to build all set, never built r
changes not built edits since the last build v, then r
built the PDFs match the settings print
Stage 5 · takes minutes

Build and print

Press r. partitor writes one PDF per part, one per group, and a large-print copy of each. A long score takes several minutes. Other services on the host keep running.

To build only some parts, type r Trombones or r 2 4. The other files stay.

The part files

The parts are in the parts folder of the item. The name starts with the part:

06-bass-trombone-Bach-Example--2026-10-0001.pdf
06-bass-trombone-Bach-Example--2026-10-0001-11x17.pdf
08-trombones-Bach-Example--2026-10-0001.pdf
  • Normal copy: Letter (or A4), double-sided.
  • Large-print copy (-11x17): print on 11×17 in (ledger) paper at 100 %. Cut at the dotted line. A4 scores give an -A3 copy instead, with no cut.

Other paper and print options: Advanced.

When something goes wrong

Common problems

You seeDo
“library folder not found”The folder does not exist. The NAS or the disk is off or not connected, or the path is wrong. Check it, wait a minute, run partitor again. See STORAGE-SMB.md.
“library folder not readable”The folder exists, but your user may not enter it (folder mode or group). Give your user read access (see INSTALL.md: the group partitor), log in again after a change of group, run partitor again.
“library folder not set up”The folder exists but has no inbox and library inside. Run the set-up again (see INSTALL.md), or point partitor at the right folder.
The wizard stopped (q, lost connection)The item is kept. Open it from the menu and continue; r asks what is still open.
A part is missing on some linesCheck the red systems on the proof; correct with t or analyse again with y.
A page shows two systems (for example 4 and 13 staves) where the score has oneAnswer j in the choices, or partitor analyse ID --join p5:4. The bar numbers of that page are then counted once.
Bar numbers are off from some line onn, then f N=B for the first wrong line.
A part rests for whole systemsNormal: those bars become one rest line with the count (for example 14), so the numbers continue.
